text: りゅうじん　さまの　ほねを　おがめる　とは！
note: りゅうじん (龍神) is the dragon god of Japanese folk belief, and おがむ is the verb for praying before something sacred, so the old man is treating the fossil as holy remains. The English line makes it just "the bones of a dragon".
claim: Ryūjin (龍神) is a dragon deity in Japanese mythology and folk religion.

check.quote: Ryūjin (龍神, lit. 'Dragon God'), which in some traditions is equivalent to Ōwatatsumi, was the tutelary deity of the sea in Japanese mythology. ... Ryūjin shinkō (竜神信仰, 'dragon god faith') is a form of Shinto religious belief that worships dragons as water kami.
